name: Teacher T
title: The Lesson-Plan Survivor
status: Active — Liberated Toad organizer and member of the Class of T
summary: Teacher T is one of the named Liberated Toads who rallied around Rodger during the Vigilance crisis. Teacher T thinks names matter because names become what frightened people repeat when they need courage. This has made Teacher T dangerously involved in the Disaster Inc. naming dispute.
description:
Teacher T survived the barrel trafficking horror and emerged with the deeply inconvenient belief that language should help people understand what is happening to them. Waluigi respects this academically while noting that most of the current situation resists lesson planning.

## The Instinct To Explain

Teacher T's response to catastrophe is not to fight it or flee it but to make it comprehensible. During and after the Vigilance crisis, Teacher T became the voice that turned raw horror into something a frightened community could hold in its head—naming what had happened, framing why, and insisting that people who understand their situation are harder to break than people who merely fear it. In a movement of survivors, this is not a soft skill. It is triage for the mind.

## Names As Weapons And Comforts

Teacher T's central conviction is that names matter because names become what frightened people repeat when they need courage. A good name steadies a shaking hand; a cruel one lodges in a child's mouth and stays there. This belief has dragged Teacher T, somewhat unwillingly, into the middle of the kingdom's pettiest and most persistent argument.

## Naming Position

Teacher T dislikes "Freeloader Zeros" because children might repeat it. Teacher T considers "Freeroamer Heroes" aspirational but possibly dishonest. Teacher T accepts "Disaster Inc." as historically accurate but wants a footnote explaining that accuracy is not endorsement. Within the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute, this makes Teacher T the closest thing the argument has to a conscience—which is precisely why nobody louder listens. Waluigi grudgingly approves the footnote.

name: Bully T
title: The Toad Who Weaponized Heckling For Morale
status: Active — Liberated Toad survivor and Class of T loudmouth
summary: Bully T is a Liberated Toad whose survival strategy appears to involve saying the thing that makes the most powerful person in the room angriest, then acting like this was tactical morale support. Waluigi does not endorse this method. Waluigi does understand it.
description:
Bully T backed Rodger during the faction's internal crisis and has since become one of the voices most likely to turn fear into noise. Sometimes that noise is useful. Sometimes it is just noise.

## The Weaponized Heckle

Bully T's survival strategy is unusual: say the thing that makes the most powerful person in the room angriest, then act as though this was tactical morale support all along. In the right moment, a well-aimed insult can shake a frightened crowd out of paralysis, puncture a tyrant's aura, or simply remind exhausted people that defiance is still an option. In the wrong moment, it is a Toad yelling at a general for no strategic reason whatsoever. Waluigi does not endorse this method. Waluigi does understand it.

## Morale By Provocation

Where Teacher T steadies people with understanding and Rodger steadies them with routine, Bully T steadies them with attitude—the loud, contagious refusal to be impressed by anyone's power. During the Liberated Toads' internal crisis, this made Bully T a reliable amplifier of whatever the practical faction needed the room to feel. It is a blunt instrument, but blunt instruments have their uses when the alternative is silence.

## Naming Position

Bully T calls the group Disaster Inc. whenever Archie can hear it, the Freeroamer Heroes whenever Waluigi can hear it, and the Freeloader Zeros whenever Wario is already mad enough that one more insult will not change the invoice. Within the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute, Bully T is not a partisan—he is an opportunist who has realized that all three names are equally effective at getting a rise out of somebody. This is not diplomacy. It is sport.

name: Nerd T
title: The Spreadsheet Toad of Brand Warfare
status: Active — Liberated Toad analyst and Class of T record keeper
summary: Nerd T is one of the Liberated Toads now tracking the Disaster Inc. naming dispute with charts, tallies, legal notes, faction reactions, and a growing confidence that nobody involved should be allowed near branding decisions.
description:
Nerd T supported Rodger during the Vigilance crisis and then made the mistake of proving useful with records. Once you prove useful with records, Waluigi notices. This is both an honor and a curse.

## The Archivist Nobody Asked For

Nerd T's contribution to the Liberated Toads is memory made rigorous. Where the community remembers its ordeal in feeling—the barrels, the Iron Legion, the fires Dan set—Nerd T remembers it in columns: who was aboard, what was traded, which numbers do not add up. In a movement forced into politics before it was ready, having someone who writes things down accurately is a quiet form of power, because the faction that controls the record controls the argument about what happened.

## Data Under Duress

What elevates Nerd T from clerk to combatant-of-a-different-kind is the refusal to let a crisis excuse sloppy accounting. Even during the Vigilance disaster, Nerd T kept tallying, on the theory that survivors would eventually need to prove what was done to them. Waluigi respects this. Evidence, unlike courage, does not fade when the adrenaline does.

## Naming Position

Nerd T has calculated that "Disaster Inc." has the strongest evidentiary accuracy, "Freeroamer Heroes" has the highest morale uplift, and "Freeloader Zeros" has the highest invoice correlation. Nerd T refuses to pick a winner until more data arrives, tracking the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute with charts, tallies, legal notes, and faction reactions, and a growing confidence that nobody involved should be allowed near branding decisions. Waluigi says the data already arrived and it says Waluigi was first.

name: Geek T
title: The Button-Maker of the Naming War
status: Active — Liberated Toad tinkerer, morale crafter, and Class of T menace
summary: Geek T is a Liberated Toad who saw three competing names for one disaster party and immediately began thinking about badges, signs, tablets, slogans, and possible merchandising. Waluigi is horrified. Wario is interested. This is the worst possible combination.
description:
Geek T survived the Vigilance and attached themself to the Liberated Toads' practical recovery work, mostly by fixing small things, labeling supplies, and turning morale into objects people can hold. This is useful. It is also how the naming dispute acquired physical merchandise.

## The Maker

Geek T is the Liberated Toads' quiet engineer of everyday function—the one who repairs the latch, labels the crate, and converts abstract community feeling into tangible, hold-in-your-hand objects. In a survivor community, this matters more than it sounds. A frightened person who is handed something solid and useful feels, briefly, that the world can still be fixed. Geek T manufactures that feeling on a small scale, one repaired object at a time.

## Merchandising A Disaster

The gift becomes a hazard when applied to the naming argument. Geek T saw three competing names for one disaster party and immediately began thinking about badges, signs, tablets, slogans, and merchandise. Waluigi is horrified. Wario is interested. Waluigi considers "horrified Waluigi plus interested Wario" the worst possible combination of reactions any idea can provoke.

## Naming Position

Geek T has made prototype buttons for Disaster Inc., the Freeroamer Heroes, and the Freeloader Zeros. The Disaster Inc. button is purple and legally superior. The Freeroamer Heroes button is heroic and annoyingly popular. The Freeloader Zeros button sold out first because Wario bought them all to hand out with bills. In this way Geek T single-handedly turned the Disaster Inc. Naming Dispute from a verbal quarrel into a physical economy, which Waluigi regards as an escalation that history will not forgive. WAH.

title: The Great Brother of Snowdin
status: Active — recorded in the Snowdin household registry

description:
Sans's taller brother and Snowdin's irrepressible puzzle guard. He treats every visitor as a future friend, every hallway as a stage, and every pot of pasta as a diplomatic instrument. Papyrus is the family's visible heart: loud, earnest, and impossible to mistake for anyone else. He answers Sans's silences by setting another place at the table.

## The Puzzle Guard of the Path

Papyrus maintains Snowdin's puzzle corridor as both a defensive line and an audition stage for future friends. Trespassers are met with a rehearsed gauntlet, a formal warning speech, and — if they show the slightest effort — a genuine offer of redemption. He patrols the outer door alongside Dedan and insists that anyone who can solve a puzzle honestly can also sit at the family table. The registry records zero prisoners taken by Papyrus and a concerning number of former enemies fed.

## Spaghetti Friday

The weekly dinner began as a household meal and became an institution. Refugees, displaced Toads, and nervous deserters from several campaigns have learned that Friday in Snowdin means a seat, a bowl, and no questions about where you slept last night. Papyrus considers this simple hospitality. The household's relief workers consider it the most stable neutral ground in the Underground, and have quietly built delivery routes around his dinner schedule. His recipe ledger is, to him, merely a notebook of who likes their noodles soft; others read it differently.

## The Brother's Keeper

Everything Papyrus does at volume is, at its quiet center, about Sans. He translates his brother's silences for strangers, defends his naps as strategy, and sets a place for him at every meal whether or not Sans appears. He does the same for every absent relative: in Papyrus's accounting, anyone missing from the table is simply late, and the household has learned not to argue with his arithmetic. He keeps every invitation ever sent to the house, filed by Grandpa Semi's system, because someone might still say yes.

## Before the Household

The chronicle's softest pages are about the years before the household grew: two young skeletons in a small house, and an older brother who built puzzle boxes to make his little brother laugh. Papyrus's first trap — a rope, a bucket, and an optimistic sign — caught nothing but Sans's attention, which was always the point. Grandpa Semi taught him that a good puzzle is a question that respects the person answering it, and Papyrus has never forgotten the lesson, even as the puzzles grew to corridor scale. The Great Papyrus persona arrived later, assembled deliberately from loudness and courage, because a small town under an enchanted sky needed someone who announced that everything would be fine and then did the work to make it true.

## The Mount Ebott Season

When the Gamma Division survey team set up at the mountain's base, Papyrus doubled his patrol schedule, reorganized the puzzle corridor for what he called 'professional visitors,' and then — because he is Papyrus — invited the survey team to dinner anyway. Dedan objected. Dedan lost. The expedition's field notes record a hostile-environment contact that became, against all protocol, a pasta dinner, and an agent who could not explain how the conversation had migrated from terrain surveys to noodle geometry. What the notes do not record is that Papyrus, between courses, asked each visitor exactly one serious question — 'are you here to help the people under the mountain, or to measure them?' — and remembered every answer. The household asked him later what he thought. He said the food was a success. He has not forgotten a single answer.

## The Recipe Ledger

The ledger sits on the kitchen shelf, unsecured, because Papyrus considers locks an insult to guests. It contains recipes, guest preferences, sauce experiments, and — in a hand that is not his — a series of delivery marks the wartime relief network once used for ciphered routing. Papyrus insists the marks are noodle notes: portion sizes, he says, for very large gatherings. The relief workers who still recognize the old cipher have agreed, formally and privately, not to disabuse him. Whether his ignorance is genuine or the finest performance in the household is the one question even Lazybones declines to answer. What is not in dispute is the result: Spaghetti Friday feeds people from several wars, and the ledger's innocent hospitality has become the most valuable neutral document in Snowdin.

## Open Questions in the Registry

The chronicle keeps a short list of Papyrus-related uncertainties, most of them affectionate. How he solved his own first puzzle, which Grandpa Semi had designed to be unsolvable, and why the old skeleton laughed for an hour afterward. Whether he knows how politically valuable his dinner table is, or whether knowing would spoil it. And the matter of the extra invitations: each season, Papyrus addresses and sends a small number of invitations to relatives no one else has heard of, in handwriting the registry cannot match. Some are returned, opened, with nothing inside but a crumb. He files every reply. He has never once seemed surprised.

## A Typical Watch

A patrol with Papyrus follows a structure he has refined over years and narrates, in full, to anyone walking beside him. First, the puzzles: each one inspected, reset, and complimented, because he maintains a puzzle left unsolved is a question left unasked, and Snowdin should ask its questions out loud. Then the perimeter, walked at his enormous stride, with a running commentary on snow quality, sight lines, and which drifts would make excellent fortifications if anyone ever needed a fort made of snow, which he hopes will be no one, but the option should exist. Visitors are challenged formally at every checkpoint and forgiven immediately. The patrol ends where it began, at the outer door, where he checks the latch twice and announces, to the door and to anyone present, that the household is safe for another rotation. Dedan, who walks the same perimeter with half the words and twice the suspicion, has said once, on the record, that the two patrols cover the same ground and none of the same threats, and that this is, reluctantly, optimal. Papyrus framed the quote. He has read it aloud to three visitors since, as if it were about pasta. It was not about pasta. Papyrus's readings of the record are, like Papyrus's invitations, final.

name: Mr. Shock
title: The Gate Guard Who Was Just a Bit Twitchy
status: Active — Legionlance gate detail; swung a shock baton at Remi and missed, and explained that anyone crossing the threshold ends up in Legion custody
summary: A guard on the gate of the Legionlance who gave his name as Mr. Shock when a girl demanded it, and did not appreciate the follow-up. He carries a shock baton, he is, in his own words, a bit twitchy, and he is the first Legion voice to tell the party the ship they came home to is 'not anymore' theirs.
description:
Remi ran at him asking his name. He asked hers and noted it sounded familiar, and asked whether she was on the wanted list. She asked his; he said Mr. Shock; she began 'Shock who—' and ducked the baton. Asked why he had done it, he said he was a bit twitchy.

He then explained the threshold: anyone who passes it ends up in custody, the Legion's, aboard the Legionlance, their top-of-the-line airship. Told it was the party's airship, he said not anymore. What happened to him after Markop swung is not on the record.

name: Rudy Lee
title: The Prosthetist Who Works While You're Awake
status: Rumoured — a town shopkeeper named him as the one person nearby who can make a prosthetic arm; not met
summary: The only prosthetist a town shopkeeper could think of when Feyward Dan asked who might fit him with an arm. 'Very hands on with their prosthetic,' and in the habit of doing the fitting while the patient is awake. The shopkeeper did not know why.
description:
Everything the archive has on Rudy Lee is one shopkeeper's rumour. Dan asked, the shopkeeper hesitated — 'there might be ONE person' — and then gave the name. Asked what 'hands on' meant, the shopkeeper said they liked to do it while the person is awake, and, asked for the reason, said they were not sure.

Dan's reply was 'doctor Rudy, got it.' Waluigi would like to point out that Dan did not ask a second question.
